questions.prompt: A machine at a large factory fills bottles with juice. To reduce the likelihood of bottles containing less than 8 ounces (oz) of juice, the machine is set to fill the bottles with a mean of $8.050 %$ of juice. To investigate whether the machine is working properly, the factory manager randomly samples ten bottles every 24 hours and records data for several variables from each of the sampled bottles. Which of the following is classified as a continuous quantitative variable for the factory manager's investigation?

options.content: Whether a randomly chosen bottle contains less than 8 oz of juice
Whether all of the bottles in the sample contain less than 8 oz of juice
The number of bottles that contain less than 8 oz of juice out of a random sample of 10 bottles of juice
The number of properly filled bottles of juice at a randomly selected time
The amount of juice, in ounces, in a randomly selected bottle

questions.prompt: According to a survey, 32 percent of people in a certain country regularly recycle. Mr. Giovanni, the mayor of a specific city in the country, wanted to know whether the residents in his city regularly recycle more than the national average. He selected a random sample of 50 residents, 28 of whom regularly recycle. Mr. Giovanni would like to use a one-sample $z$-test for a population proportion to test the hypotheses $H_{0}: p=0.32$ versus $H_{a}: p>0.32$, where $p$ is the proportion of city residents who regularly recycle. In order to use this test, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion needs to be approximately normal. Which of the following is true for Mr. Giovanni's study and ensures that the sampling distribution of the sample proportion is approximately normal?

options.content: The distribution of the population of all residents who regularly recycle is approximately normal.
The sample size is 50 , which is larger than 30 .
The sample size of 50 is less than $10 %$ of the residents in the city.
The expected number of residents who regularly recycle is 16, and the expected number of residents who do not regularly recycle is 34 , and both numbers are at least 10 .
The observed number of residents who regularly recycle is 28 , and the observed number of residents who do not regularly recycle is 22 , and both numbers are at least 10 .
